newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker, Oct reaches new high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker, Oct reaches new high.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed lower, having set its range before midday and then drifting on both sides of unchanged for the remainder of the session.

Trading sources said follow-through fund buying buoyed the benchmark October contract to a new high of 11.75 cents, where producer selling emerged to pressure the spot month below unchanged and to the day's low of 11.61 cents.

Firm support was seen at 11.60 cents, and sell stops are rumored to be resting at 11.57 cents in October. A move below that key price could send October to its next downside target of 11.55-11.50 cents, traders said.
The most-active October contract closed down 0.04 cent at 11.66 cent a lb, having ranged from a new contract high of 11.75 cents, to 11.61 cents.
Second-position March settled 0.09 lower at 11.86 cents, while the rest of the board finished down 0.05 and 0.06 cent.
An estimated 19,668 lots changed hands on the day compared with Monday's official 16,078 lots.
Resistance was pegged at the contract high of 11.78 cents in October, but traders said the contract has probably set its near-term high and expect prices to ease toward support on Wednesday.
Open interest in October fell 147 lots to 111,590 lots as of early Monday.
March gained 1,045 lots to stand at 55,685 lots.
The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) said world sugar output could reach 122.2 million tonnes raw value in the 1997/98 season, leaving a deficit of 1.0 million tonnes.
Consumption was pegged at 123.2 million tonnes for the season.
